Procedures for water breaks on the job
Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and this page walks new staff through why

At the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, water breaks are part of steady, humane service. When the desk stays busy, you may feel tempted to push through, but a brief reset helps you stay clear, calm, and accurate with passengers and handlers. That matters when animals are waiting to travel, because your tone, your memory, and your patience all shape the experience.

Watch the flow at the desk and use a quiet moment to step away before you get overheated or unfocused. Keep your own bottle in the approved area, and make sure the desk is covered before you leave. If a passenger is mid-check-in, finish the current step, pass the file to the senior coordinator if needed, and then take the break cleanly. Do not rush back in half-alert, since missed details can affect crate notes, carrier checks, and boarding guidance.

When you return, wash or sanitize your hands before touching paperwork, terminals, or animal handling items. If you were speaking with a traveler, pick up the thread with a calm voice and a simple recap. This helps passengers feel looked after and keeps the desk organized. If the station feels hot, crowded, or tense, say so early to the team lead rather than waiting until you are worn down. Small honesty keeps everyone safer.

Remember that water breaks are not a luxury. They support steady judgment, kind service, and reliable records across the whole shift. What to remember is simple: pause early, cover the desk, return cleanly, and keep your work calm.
